_comment: Record of the last independent cross-check of deploy/sandbox.Dockerfile's pinned pandoc / Chrome-for-Testing sha256 digests. Regenerate by bumping PANDOC_VERSION/CHROME_FOR_TESTING_VERSION in the Dockerfile, then re-running scripts/verify-pinned-checksums.sh and pasting its output into this file. tests/test_pinned_checksum_verification.py asserts this file's versions and hashes stay in lockstep with deploy/sandbox.Dockerfile, so a version bump without an updated record fails CI instead of silently going unverified. See SECURITY.md ('Known follow-ups') for the full writeup.

wolfi_base_image.method: OCI image-index digest resolved from cgr.dev's registry v2 API (Docker-Content-Digest header, Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json), cross-checked by re-fetching the raw index manifest body and computing its sha256 locally -- both produced the same digest. The index resolves linux/amd64 to sha256:73f2cab0f11208427595d4bdd784046bc4116ef7cc52f0c1b48b6b7f820288d5 and linux/arm64 to sha256:742cb89fddcad855188f892183ded0b4dcb48d83fdb41ed4463bbab2fe3f7801. The arm64 image installed current python-3.11 and py3.11-pip, ran `import math`, and created and executed a venv.
wolfi_base_image.source_query: curl -sSI -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json' https://cgr.dev/v2/chainguard/wolfi-base/manifests/latest | grep -i docker-content-digest; docker buildx imagetools inspect --raw cgr.dev/chainguard/wolfi-base:latest | shasum -a 256
wolfi_base_image.note: Chainguard rebuilds wolfi-base frequently; re-resolve and re-pin this digest (and update this record's verified_at) when intentionally moving to a newer base. Pinning all Dockerfiles to one shared digest keeps them building the same base until that deliberate bump.

pandoc.method: GitHub Releases API per-asset `digest` field (sha256, computed server-side by GitHub at upload time -- independent of the maintainer who recorded the Dockerfile pin), cross-checked against a fresh independent download of the same release asset.

chrome_for_testing.method: Chrome for Testing manifests list linux64 and linux-arm64 assets for both chrome and chrome-headless-shell at this version, and the pinned version is the current Stable release in last-known-good-versions-with-downloads.json. The manifests publish URLs but no checksum fields. For each architecture, the fresh asset sha256 is checked against the Dockerfile pin and its md5 against Google Cloud Storage's server-reported x-goog-hash header.
